slides.teacher_cue: New sound — /z/. Voiced alveolar fricative. Same position as /s/ but with voicing. Hand on throat: /s/ silent, /z/ vibrates. zip, buzz, jazz. Important note: the letter s also makes /z/ in many words you already know. is = /ɪz/. his = /hɪz/. has = /hæz/. was = /wɒz/. These are not new — you have been reading them since Lesson 2. Now you know why they sound the way they do.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /z/ cleanly as a voiced alveolar fricative and understand that s can also make /z/.
slides.correction_move: Model /s/ vs /z/ with hand on throat. Students alternate. Then review: is, his, has, was — students confirm the /z/ in each. Connect to previous knowledge.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /s/ substitution and for b/v confusion — /z/ is the voiced counterpart of /s/, same as v is to f and b is to p.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect z to one strong word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students say z clearly and connect it to a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Say zip — to fasten with a zip. Confirm /z/ onset. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say zip orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model zip orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /s/ substitution at onset.

slides.teacher_cue: Mime a bee buzzing. Say buzz — zz at the end is one sound. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say buzz orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model buzz orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the zz spelling — two letters, one sound /z/. Final voiced fricative.

slides.teacher_cue: Say jazz — a style of music. jz double ending. Confirm /dʒ/ onset and /z/ coda. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say jazz orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model jazz orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the jz pattern and for /z/ at the end.

slides.teacher_cue: Say fizz — the bubbles in a drink. Confirm /f/ onset and zz coda. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say fizz orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model fizz orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /p/ on /f/ and for the zz spelling.

slides.teacher_cue: Say zoom — to move very fast. Confirm /z/ onset and long /uː/ vowel team. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say zoom orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model zoom orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /s/ on /z/ and for long /uː/ in oo.

slides.observation_note: Watch for /kw/ onset and for /z/ at the end — quiz is now fully decodable.
